One section per decision, headed `## D<n>（简称）`, ordered as in the index table of [decisions.md](decisions.md); the line at the top of each section, `**现状**：`, is taken from the "Status" and "Conclusion (brief)" cells of that index row, and the rest of the section is every change made to it: blocks by date in reverse order, one `#### ` subheading per change, with the body giving before, after and basis. A change that names several decisions has a copy in each of those sections, with the same content. How it is organized and how to add an entry follow `.claude/rules/changelog-format.md`.

⚠️ Item numbers in entries are always today's numbers: since 2026-08-30 each decision's items have only one numbering, and on that date entries earlier than that day were rewritten to match. What status an item had at the time is given by that entry's own before, after and basis.

### 2026-09-06

- D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index) grows five items from "no items" (user ruling); the semantics of D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) settled item 3 close accordingly
  - **Conclusion**: the user ruling grows five items: the criterion for what may enter the self-contained section, the reverse index is self-contained data, extension-point semantics, the classification criterion, and one unique reference each

  - **D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index)** before had only one sentence, "a reverse index is required, designed into the format on day 1", plus a section of research on bucket generation, with no items;
    after, all five are user rulings:
    ① **What may enter the self-contained section** — any data "specific to this unit and **immutable**" may enter; by default it goes in, not trimmed;
    ② **The reverse index is self-contained data** — the body of the reverse mapping is already in the unit; "taking the authoritative state" does not add a fourth entry to the authoritative state list but acknowledges it is already in the first entry (the unit);
    ③ **Reserve a customizable extension point**, with one of two semantics: either empty or a reference, **no inline data**;
    ④ **The self-contained section and the extension point are split by "does it change with the version"** — what does not change goes into the self-contained section, what may differ per version goes into the extension point;
    ⑤ **Self-contained immutable data and mutable extension data each carry exactly one reference**; once the new version is written the old one is disconnected, and the disconnection is done by the tree without changing the old unit.
  - **The criterion of ① is more fundamental than the existing forbidden list**: D18 (Information Carried in a Block) settled item 3 keeps out physical placement on the grounds that it is "not authenticated, can be silently tampered with",
    whereas by the criterion of ① physical placement **is not immutable data at all** (blocks get moved, and D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index) exists precisely so they can be moved) ⇒ it cannot even get in the door.
    ⚠️ File names and separator keys are the class that is "immutable yet still not allowed in", on the grounds of the leakage surface (D9 (Encryption) settled item 5); **that prohibition must stay separately**.
  - **The two class names of ⑤ were decided by the user** (the main agent's "ownership chain / version chain" was rejected because a chain is only one thing living inside, not the class itself; the current two names map directly onto the "does it change with the version" criterion of settled item 4). **Three restrictions were written down**: the "unique" of the self-contained immutable data's reference means the birth owner, not all current referrers (otherwise it would be read as not supporting sharing);
    the number of protected generations is set by the K of I-7.4 (Blocks in Recent K Generations Not Reused), K ≤ root ring depth, root ring R = 3 ⇒ at most 3 generations, which is a different number from "how many generations the chain can walk";
    **that reference does not constitute a reference**: sweep acceptance ignores it, and expiry relies on comparing the target's birth generation number, not on cleanup (the unit is immutable, the extension point's bytes cannot be erased).
  - **D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) settled item 3**: before, it settled only "the reference must not overlap core-layer main fields" and "the length need not be specified";
    after, it records that the semantics are settled (authoritative record in D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index) settled item 3): either empty or a reference, no inline data
    ⇒ from then on this item owes only the byte form, no longer "what goes in". **Status still unsettled.**
- D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index) adds a sixth item (stack of generation data and release boundary), and moves the research to a "for reference" section at the end
  - **Conclusion**: new settled item 6 (stack of generation data and release boundary); the research moves to the end for reference; the sentence on who needs this decision stays at the top of the body

  - **New D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index) settled item 6 (user ruling)**: the generation data in the extension point is a **stack of depth 5**; writing a new version **copies and shifts forward** (the unit is immutable, so push cannot be an in-place append);
    on expiry gc releases the whole batch; **the fs does not keep old versions implicitly**; **backup is not the fs's business**.
    "Expiry" hangs on two settled gates: what is referenced by a snapshot goes into the deadlist, not defer, per D3 (Space Allocation) settled item 7, and is released only when the snapshot is destroyed;
    the latest K generations must not be reused (I-7.4 (Blocks in Recent K Generations Not Reused), K ≤ root ring depth = 3)
   ⇒ the accurate reading of "all reclaimed in the next reclamation cycle" is "all those **not referenced by any root (including snapshots) and already past K generations**" (confirmed by the user).
    ⚠️ **The word "implicitly" in "does not keep implicitly" is a qualifier and cannot be dropped** — a snapshot is itself "keeping old versions for a long time",
    and it is the reason the whole deadlist machinery of D5 (Snapshot / Space Accounting Mechanism) exists; drop "implicitly" and this directly conflicts with D5 (Snapshot / Space Accounting Mechanism) / D6 (Snapshot Implementation Model).

- D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index) adds two clarifications and one boundary; D18 (Information Carried in a Block) writes the same boundary
  - **Conclusion**: adding "unique means chain-unique" resolves the contradiction; the division of labor where settled item 4 sets the criterion and settled item 3 sets the form is spelled out; one sentence on each side of the boundary between the two decisions

  - **Settled item 5 adds "unique = chain-unique"** (user clarification): every new data unit starts a unique chain —
    new data generated ⇒ old chain disconnected ⇒ new link completed. ⇒ **No contradiction** with the "stack of depth 5" of settled item 6:
    the stack is that unique chain **materialized to 5 levels**, the k-th being the k-th predecessor.
    Before, the body said only "unique", which literally contradicted settled item 6; the main agent had not reconciled it when writing.
  - **Settled item 4 adds its division of labor with settled item 3**: settled item 4 decides "what should go into the extension point" (criterion), settled item 3 decides "how it is expressed once inside" (form) —
    a mutable value is also stored as a reference. ⇒ The extension point is normally **not empty**; "either empty" means empty is **allowed**.
    Before, the two items sat side by side and read as if "mutable data may enter" and "only a reference may be stored" were mutually exclusive.
  - **New boundary between D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index) and D18 (Information Carried in a Block), one sentence on each side** (user ruling “hard-code the boundary, don't let it get muddled”):

- Three places together withdraw the basis "the extension point is within checksum / authentication coverage" (D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index), D18 (Information Carried in a Block), D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States))
  - **Conclusion**: withdrawn in all three places together, replaced by the basis that it does not constitute a reference and forgery only points the lead at nothing, written in the scope paragraph of D18 (Information Carried in a Block) settled item 3

  - **Before**: the scope paragraph of D18 (Information Carried in a Block) settled item 3, D1 (Data Mobility / Reverse Index) settled item 4 and D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) settled item 3 all used
    "the extension point is within the whole unit's checksum / authentication coverage (hard constraint 1)" as the basis.
    **After, all three withdraw it together**, stating why it may not be used again: it is **mutually exclusive** with D3 (Space Allocation) point 4, "the keyless side **can move**" —
    with encryption on, "authentication" is the MAC, and the MAC covers the ciphertext; being within coverage means the extension point is ciphertext the keyless side cannot read,
    while resident automatic compaction is a hard commitment. Only one of the two can stay, and the one kept is **can move**.
  - **Replacement basis (written in the scope paragraph of D18 (Information Carried in a Block) settled item 3, the other two places point to it)**: a physical reference in the extension point does not hit the forbidden list,

    if the upper bound followed the device count, the device count is a volatile input (losing a disk does not go through the drain barrier of settled item 4 b); a constant closes the value set to `{2,3,4}` so the branches can be tested.
  - **Measurement**: E63 (How Many Columns Allocator Writes per Invocation). Including write volume in the criterion saves 61% (90% for small writes); upper bound 4 versus no upper bound
    differs by only 13% in space, while the expected data loss for a double-disk failure is 10.7% vs 25.0%, and the failure mode changes from "partially damaged" to diffuse (per-stripe hit rate 1.000).

    (per-stripe hit rate vs per-capacity overhead). The expected data-loss fraction in consistent units is `(w−1)/C(D,2)`, linear, and equal weighting gives **6**.
    ⇒ 4 is kept as the **more conservative** side, but that arithmetic **is not load-bearing**; it is written into the body's "three unknowns that must be stated".
  - ⚠️ **Equal-weight λ has no source in the kb**; **it holds only for parity=1** (the redundancy form of D16 (Publish Semantics) is still a gap).
  - **The backward leg pointed out the original text required all three together** ⇒ this time only a and the upper bound are settled; **the participating device subset is split off into new item 8**.

  - **Conclusion**: user ruling: pick the group from the emptiest g disks and within the group take the emptiest w; the group is not stored on disk but derived from position entries; rebalancing re-lands whole groups per object; all eight items of D2 (RAID Stripe Policy) settled, the main conclusion of variable stripe width unchanged.

    when a disk in the group fills up, re-choose; `g` is a constant declared in the system configuration, initial value 4; **the group is not stored on disk** and is derived from the union of device identities in position entries;
    the rebalance of settled item 4 c **moves per object, re-landing the whole group**.
  - **All 8 items of D2 (RAID Stripe Policy) settled**; the main conclusion "stripe width is variable, every write is a full-stripe write, never read-modify-write" unchanged.
  - **Basis**: E67 (Which Disks a Stripe Spans) (exhaustive over all 28 failed-disk pairs). How much data is lost does not depend on the selection method (all six arms equal cell by cell at 3/28);
    the selection method decides how the loss is distributed — with group binding 78.6% of objects are completely unharmed, with rotation only 14.3%.
    After adding a disk, moving whole objects keeps the theoretical value 83.3%, while moving per stripe drops to 75.0% ⇒ the basis for the move-granularity point.

    local "reject", but its counterexample (could be pinned to four small disks) **was falsified by the heterogeneous-capacity round's measurement**.
    ⚠️ The local vote's output contained spliced corrupted words and counts as flawed.
  - ⚠️ **Two stated unknowns**: per-object parallelism is capped at `g` (E67 (Which Disks a Stripe Spans) did not measure it, while the D25 (Target Workload Priority) primary workload is large sequential files);

  - **Conclusion**: measured by E74 (Allocation Record Entry Count and Compaction Cost): the tree itself eats about 0.055% of capacity; on the compaction side the number of placements is fixed and the number of rewritten nodes grows only with tree height; COW amplification differs 370 times when scattered.

  - **Before**: “⚠️ **The cost has not been measured**: per-placement means the entry count of allocation records grows with capacity……
    its interaction with ‘resident background compaction’ (compaction rewrites placement ownership in bulk) has not been measured.”
  - **After**: the relation between entry count and capacity now has absolute values — **this tree itself eats about 0.055% of capacity**
    (483 million entries / 9.0 GiB on 16 TiB; 7.7 billion entries / 145 GiB on 256 TiB);
    indeed of a different unit from the accounting tree. On the compaction side: with a fixed 4096 placements and capacity growing 256 times,
    the number of rewritten nodes only goes from 13 to 19 (all from tree height) ⇒ **no term grows with disk capacity**.
    ⚠️ It also records something unexpected: **COW rewrites the whole 16 KiB node**;
    amplification is 2.6 times when placements are contiguous and 964 times when scattered, **a 370-fold difference**;
    the key of settled item 3 (device identity + in-device offset) puts compaction at the good end.
  - **Basis**: E74 (Allocation Record Entry Count and Compaction Cost) measurements.

   52: - 代价是空间放大，恒等式，全部落在小文件上；已定项 1 取 32 KiB 把小文件的补齐浪费恰好翻倍。这与「省空间不是目标」（`.claude/rules/fs-design.md`）不冲突——那条禁的是拿「比谁省」当判据，不是禁止记下一个绝对代价。空间放大会经 D5（快照 / 空间记账机制） 的记账进入 ENOSPC 准入，那是运行时决策路径，不是纸面数字。
   53: - 补齐之后小文件怎么落：写路径上把多个文件打包进一个单元出局——I/O 上没有一格赢，只买空间，而空间不是判据。⚠️ 这一句只在单次操作口径下成立：E66（补齐之后小文件怎么落） 的打包臂每写一个小对象都读回整个容器，没量「一次事务里写同一单元上的多个小文件」那一格（C168（E66 的 pack 臂只覆盖最差的一种实现））。写路径之外由后台整理把小对象搬进共享容器，是 D27（小数据打包容器） 的事，写入时照旧按已定项 2 补齐；内联阈值由 D14（双轨（大小文件 / 持久临时）） 已定项 3 定成 0，判据是原子性。
   54: - 内联的读侧优势 E66（补齐之后小文件怎么落） 量不准：它给内联记了索引叶那 16 KiB，却没给 extent 记同一次叶读，对称记法下内联赢 54.5%（叶不命中）到 100%（叶命中），不是不对称记法显示的一成半；打平读写比同样不许当一个数用，可观测区间 5:1 ~ 13.5:1（随设备状态），再叠上索引节点缓存命中率，下界掉到 0.42:1。E66（补齐之后小文件怎么落） 的内联臂不建模扇出下降，给出的是内联代价的下界。反方向是 E8（大文件与小文件是否该走不同写路径） 量到的扫描 6.2 倍（内联把 inode 记录撑大 ⇒ 叶子数暴涨）；两个实验量的不是同一种读（点读 vs 扫描），不许把「内联点读快 10%」读成「内联更好」。补齐没有改变 E8（大文件与小文件是否该走不同写路径） 的结论。
   58: - E65（校验和粒度的写侧代价） 的 `pad` 臂（纯算术，恒等式）——1 KiB 文件在 16 KiB / 32 KiB 单元下占 16 倍 / 32 倍，4 KiB 占 4 倍 / 8 倍，单元大小减一占 1.00006 倍 / 1.00003 倍。
   59: - E66（补齐之后小文件怎么落）——补齐之后三条落法（N=5，两条对照过）：独立 extent（补齐）点读与写都是基准（按新文件首次写建模，不读旧单元），1 KiB 文件占 32 倍；内联进 16 KiB 节点写贵 861–906%；多文件打包进一个单元，读与 extent 逐档相同（差 ±1.06%）、写贵 1076–1106%；后两条空间紧凑。
   60: - 用户定案（日期与经过在变更史）。
   70: - 新分配的单元没有旧内容可读。「走 RMW」在这一格有两种落法：真的去读那个物理位置的残留（读到的是别人的死数据，无语义），或者把新分配单元的旧内容定义为全零、因而不发那次读（与 I-2.3（补齐字节为零且参与校验和） 同向，且不付那一次读回）。条款没有区分这两种，留给写实现的人定。`crates/` 里今天只有整份内容的写：`publish_first_file` / `publish_overwrite`（`crates/singlefs-core/src/transaction.rs:1135` / `:1190`）收的是文件的整份内容，`build_data_unit`（`crates/singlefs-core/src/unit.rs:226`）在零缓冲上现装一个新单元，不读旧单元，也不读落点——新文件那一次写的行为与「定义为全零」那一种相同；改既有单元其中一段的部分写，`crates/` 里没有（`grep -rniE 'rmw|read_modify|读—改—写|部分写' crates --include=*.rs` 零命中）。
   71: - RMW 引入一条新的失败耦合：旧单元读不回来或 MAC 验不过时，连「只想改其中 4 KiB」的写也做不成——重算整单元的 MAC 需要那 28 KiB 的原文。该怎么办由已定项 4 定：那个写失败并返错，不许用零填充重建。
   72: - 引写侧代价时写明口径：字节倍数与时间倍数差一个数量级（字节恒 8 倍而时间只涨一成多），不许混用；含 AES 的总倍数不许直接引用；「NVMe 把写吸进 SLC」这个解释已作废——`rmw` 与 `full` 两条臂没有任何持久点，`O_DIRECT` 写只等到设备缓冲 ack，量到的是 PCIe 传输加固定命令开销，与介质无关。
   73: - E65（校验和粒度的写侧代价） 按「一次操作一个单元」计，是上界不是预期值：真实写路径会把多个改动并进一次发布（D16（发布语义）），摊销没有建模。
   77: - E65（校验和粒度的写侧代价）——32 KiB 单元下写 4 KiB 用户数据（真 NVMe，N=5，两条对照全过）：字节写放大恒为 8 倍（绝对值断言钉死）；不 `fdatasync` 219643.7 ns/op，比 16 KiB 贵 15.76%，设备侧 12.51%；每次 `fdatasync` 472393.6 ns/op，贵 8.16%，设备侧 6.63%；整单元新建写（`full` 臂，不读）33917.3 ns/op，贵 25.92%，其中 11 个百分点是 AES，设备侧只有 14.53%（fio 3.36 独立复现设备侧为 1.136）。`fdatasync` 在本机是 250–310 μs 的、与 G 无关的固定开销（`rmwsync − rmw` 逐档 263/267/247/253/258/247 μs，字节涨 32 倍而它不升反略降），它把粒度差摊掉。
   78: - E66（补齐之后小文件怎么落）——首次写不读回的代价：4 KiB 档设备侧中位数，新文件首次写（`extent` 臂，纯写 32768 字节）25018 ns，读回整个 32 KiB 单元再写（`pack` 臂，32768 读 + 32768 写）299190 ns；多出来的是那一次设备往返，不是字节。

  109: - 代价照实记：净荷不是 2 的幂。用户数据粒度 = `32768 − 头 − 扩展点声明值 N`，文件偏移 → 单元要做除法而不是移位，且 N 随每条线声明而变。这笔代价换到的是一条更硬的东西：单元大小是一个常量，不随头长度或 N 变 ⇒ 分配器、根槽对齐、`physical_block_size` 整除关系都只对一个数负责。
  110: - 读路径上还有两层代价，条款不动：净荷 32768 − 头不是 4096 的整数倍 ⇒ 文件的 4 KiB 页有 (4096 − gcd(4096, P)) / P ≈ 12.5% 跨在两个单元上，读一页要读两个单元；净荷从偏移 h 起 ⇒ 页缓存页 / O_DIRECT 缓冲拿不到零拷贝。随机页读与顺序读两格反向，按跑前写死的判据只报交叉点：随机页读占用户字节 1.0%–1.5% 以上时补齐形态更省，以下含头更省；D25（目标负载优先级） 没有数值权重，不据此重开已定项 5。

  the AAD table of D9 (Encryption) settled item 4, the cross-snapshot partial-overwrite fragments of D6 (Snapshot Implementation Model),
  and the width budget of D19 (Block Pointer Structure & Width Budget) — reading as if the first version already produced sub-unit sharing.

  **After**: **splitting is a reserved feature, off in the first version, `extent_off` is always 0, and each unit always has exactly one nonce and one MAC.**
  The wording of those four places all changed from present tense to conditional ("if splitting is enabled"), each stating what the first version actually looks like:
  cross-snapshot partial overwrite goes through whole-unit COW (D6 (Snapshot Implementation Model)); the value range is [0, 32768), 15 bits suffice,
  and it is always 0 in the first version (D19 (Block Pointer Structure & Width Budget)); those bits are kept because of the "fixed width with reserved bits" policy,
  not because the first version uses them (D9 (Encryption)). This ruling **does not change the bytes of new-pool file creation** —
  the fixed width with reserved bits of D19 (Block Pointer Structure & Width Budget) settled item 3 means those 2 bytes are occupied whether used or not;
  what it changes is "whether one MAC gets copied into k copies".

  **Basis**: user ruling, plus agreement of all three legs of the three-way argument. The forward leg (sonnet) judged
  survives-with-amendment; **the backward attack leg (opus) conceded on its own** — it held that the whole-unit read-modify-write of D4 (Checksum Location) settled item 3
  already blocks splitting, and it found no counterexample reachable by the first version; the local leg (counterexample hunting)
  walked through reflink, dedup, RAID rebuild, journal replay, snapshot destruction, restriping and tombstone packing one by one,
  and reported "not a single one". The two cloud legs also jointly issued a batch of must-checks, which I verified against the original text: reflink is a day-1 commitment,
  but what it shares is a whole unit with offset always 0, which is reference sharing, not splitting; the form of packing at sub-unit granularity
  has been rejected by D14 (Dual-Track: Large/Small Files & Persistent/Transient), and E66 (How Small Files Land After Padding) also judged it out;
  the D2 (RAID Stripe Policy) rebalance moves "a whole object as a group" (settled item 8);
  the tombstone units of D18 (Information Carried in a Block) are metadata, not data extents.
  The three legs' raw outputs are archived in `research/prompts/c72-extent-split-*.md`.

  **A rider attached, from the trap the backward leg pointed out**: the reason in D9 (Encryption) settled item 4 for excluding `extent_off` from the AAD
  **changed to first stating "the field composition of the AAD is a permanent day-1 contract"**, no longer "it is always 0 in the first version, so putting it in is harmless".
  The latter would let a future editor put it back into the AAD on the grounds that "it's 0 anyway", and once splitting is enabled

  while the narrow reading passes all four cells (tightest 53% of the budget). **The two point the same way but are not the same**: the cost side alone cannot pick an answer (expensive is not wrong),
  and the definition side alone has no quantity.

- The cost of multiple writable heads measured: a difference of kind, not of multiple
  - **Conclusion**: after scanning scales, the difference is the kind difference of constant 0 versus O(N); the same round also ruled that the system configuration tree table is an open list on day 1.

  - **The multiple-writable-heads candidate of D6 (Snapshot Implementation Model) has its cost measured** ([experiments.md](experiments.md)
    E26 (Lookup Cost and Accuracy of Three Accounting Models), three rounds byte-identical):
    under linear topology the accounting form depended on **does zero lookups at all 6 scale tiers**;
    under multiple writable heads it grows with the total number of extents, **log-log slope 1.32** (exact reference counting 0.95).
    ⇒ **The difference is not a multiple like "13 versus 23" but a kind like "constant 0" versus "O(N)".**
  - ⚠️ **The way the first version of E26 (Lookup Cost and Accuracy of Three Accounting Models) was written misled the reading**: it reported only the absolute value of a toy world of 64 snapshots × 8 extents
    (13 lookups), which read as "the cost is not high". After scanning scales the conclusion flipped.
    **The absolute values were changed to scaling; both the body and the decision changed.**
  - **The btrfs numbers (+76% / +1347% / −25%) are not remeasured**, for a mechanistic reason:
    the root of btrfs qgroup's slowness is its own backref resolution, which this project's design does not have.
    [prior-art.md](prior-art.md) long marked it "not to be taken as this project's performance expectation" — that mark was right.
  - **One measurement basis pinned**: the `owner_ref` arm of E26 (Lookup Cost and Accuracy of Three Accounting Models) **is not btrfs squota**.
    squota only handles quota ownership and does not take part in liveness judgment; getting it wrong only makes quotas inaccurate;
    moving that mechanism over to make release judgments would misrelease (measured with multiple writable heads + 70% sharing, all 8 misreleased, the data-loss direction).
    **The two may not cite each other.**
  - **D15 (Format Freeze Policy) settled item 2 settled (user ruling)**: the system configuration tree table is an open list on day 1.
    The basis is in D15 (Format Freeze Policy)'s own judgment table — under an open list, a new keyspace is only "cannot see the new tree" (compat) to old readers,
    while hard-coding gives "cannot read the tree table" (incompat). That row of the judgment table is pinned as compat.

  - **Conclusion**: a new discipline added, not sacrificing self-containment to save space; all five items ruled; the decision index table adds a conclusion brief column.

  **A new project-local discipline (user ruling)**: `.claude/rules/fs-design.md` adds
  "**do not sacrifice self-containment to save space**" — self-describing data had better be written larger, unless measurement proves the saved part is a bottleneck.
  The reason is that the costs on the two sides are asymmetric: what is saved is space; what is given up is "whether a unit picked up on its own can still prove itself".

  **Five rulings**:

  - **D8 (Core Index Structure) settled item 1 — settled: take idempotent full values, accept the rise in key count.**
    Basis (user ruling): E14 (Discriminative Power of I-3.1: Idempotent Full Value vs Incremental Delta) measured both sides —
    idempotent caught 3/3, incremental Δ **0/4** (all four kinds of semantic bugs got the ledger wrong while the checks stayed all green).
    ⚠️ It also makes cost 1 of D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) **not hold in this project** (cost 2 unaffected).
  - **D9 (Encryption) settled item 4 — settled: nonce stored per extent, not computed on the spot.**
    Basis (user ruling): the nonce is something that should be pinned at the moment of writing; a parallel reason is the new discipline "do not sacrifice self-containment to save space".
    Cost 12 bytes / logical extent. ⚠️ It dismantles the keystream reuse chain of E35 (Two Forms of Multi-Writable-Heads),
    but brings a **new obligation**: nonce generation must guarantee no collision between two writable heads — **this inference did not go through three-way, nor was the stored-nonce arm of E35 (Two Forms of Multi-Writable-Heads) rerun**.
  - **D18 (Information Carried in a Block) settled item 3 — settled: data blocks carry a plaintext self-describing header, with the fields being the five AAD ones of D9 (Encryption) settled item 6.**
    Basis (user ruling): these fields exist to be obtained quickly, the faster the better; and the new discipline requires writing larger.
    **Zero new leakage surface** (D9 (Encryption) settled item 5 already settled a plaintext reverse index; the same tuple is already in plaintext),
    **zero new integrity mechanism** (those five fields are already authenticated in the AAD; changing them makes decryption fail).
    Two lines not to cross: no physical placement / device ID; no file name / separator key.
  - **D19 (Block Pointer Structure & Width Budget) settled item 3 — settled: fixed width, bits kept when unencrypted.**
    Basis (user ruling, a direct application of the new discipline). **Also answering the user's question "doesn't elastic expansion make this a non-issue?" — no**:
    incompat bits govern "whether the reader knows this layout", not "how a pointer is encoded internally within the same layout";
    and per the format branch criterion of `.claude/rules/fs-design.md`, swapping fixed width for variable length **buys no improvement in failure modes**,
    only bytes, while that criterion expressly forbids "faster / smaller" from appearing. The cost has been computed: unencrypted it wastes 28 bytes / logical extent
    (0.68% for a 4 KiB extent, 0.17% at 16 KiB, 0.021% at 128 KiB; arithmetic, not measured).
  - **D22 (Synthesizing Unit Atomicity) settled item 5 wording corrected**: "completed" changed to "settled", consistent with elsewhere.

  **Two directions settled, pending experiments** (both still marked "blocking the first line of transaction-layer code"):

  - **D23 (Journal Role & Format) settled item 8: the record header adds a reverse chain.** Basis (user ruling): the byte cost is small,
    and it buys both telling timelines apart and traversal independence. ⚠️ Effectiveness unproven; experiment placement E39 (Does Reverse Chain Block Remnant Records).

  — the sentence in D15 (Format Freeze Policy) describing the pointer field layout, whose parenthetical content is part of the sentence itself, confirmed and kept.

    after: take A, **and withdraw the half sentence "or reclaim blocks" in settled item 5**,
    changing to "allocate only within the handover area issued by the key side, and mark dead in the plaintext mapping";
    basis: the necessary and sufficient condition for alias immunity is "the plaintext side's free set is at all times a subset of the authoritative free set",
    which the keyless side cannot compute itself (the complement of the plaintext mapping is not the free set; the difference contains the journal ring, root ring,
    blocks pending reuse within the replay window, acceptance reservations, and pending-deletion intent occupancy); the only feasible path is a handover area issued by the key side and
    covered by the master key MAC. B, once stripped of the ability to "turn occupied into free", is no longer a free table but a lease credential.
  - **The fork itself was wrong before**: A's original text said "does not touch encrypted accounting", which literally **cannot even relocate** —
    relocation also needs a destination, and the free judgment of the destination can likewise come only from the plaintext side.

### 2026-08-28

- D9 (Encryption) settled item 2 ruled: MAC takes the full 128 bits, not truncated.
  - **Conclusion**: D9 (Encryption) settled item 2 ruled: MAC takes the full 128 bits, not truncated.
  - **Conclusion**: changed to: zero implementation precedent supports not truncating; the contradiction rewritten as no separate tree layer but indeed two fields; a new debt recorded that total pointer width exceeds 256 bits.

  - **D9 (Encryption) settled item 2 ruled: MAC takes the full 128 bits, not truncated** / basis: the three-way argument agreed.
    ChaCha20-Poly1305 on Linux enforces exactly 16 bytes; the allowed set of SP 800-38D §5.2.1.2 does not include 80 (SHALL level);
    zero implementations pin a cap on forgery attempts; the cost is 8 bytes / 4 KiB extent, amortized 0.195%;
    and this project has settled "two integrity fields" ⇒ the MAC is left only with authentication duty, and truncation buys no detection capability.
  - **The original D9 (Encryption) criterion overturned**, "depends on whether the read retry cap can be pinned" / basis: zero implementation precedent,
    and the standard's means against unbounded attempts is keeping the full tag, not bounding the number of attempts.
    That criterion also **cited the wrong document**: `MaxInvalids` belongs to SP 800-38B, not 38D (verified on the local PDFs: 38B 2 hits, 38D 0 hits),
    and Appendix C of 38D counts "all decryption invocations, including successful ones". ⇒ C3 (read retries lack hard upper bound) can be written off, the reason being its premise's measurement basis was wrong.
  - **The contradiction between D4 (Checksum Location) and D9 (Encryption) settled item 1 reconciled**: D4 (Checksum Location) originally said "two values of the same field……encryption opens no separate layer",
    while D9 (Encryption) settled item 1 settled "the pointer has two integrity fields" / basis: the two were mutually exclusive and both marked settled,
    and kb-discipline's "one fact has only one authoritative record" failed here. Rewritten as "no separate **tree** layer, but indeed two fields".
  - **New debt**: the settled items of total pointer width add up to 264–296 bits, exceeding ZFS's 256-bit slot;
    and the node size conclusion of E7 (Offline Index Harness) was run without these encryption fields, **it must be rerun with the final pointer width**.
  - Two things not to be miscited recorded: Ferguson's GCM disaster does not extrapolate to Poly1305 (that is the linear structure of GHASH);
    the MUST NOT of RFC 8439 is an unanalyzed conservative prohibition, and neither BoringSSL nor OpenSSL enforces it.
    But **the argument for the danger of truncation stands independently**: the WC bound is fℓ/2^τ with a message length factor,
    one successful forgery on Poly1305 likewise exposes r (DJB naclcrypto §9 verbatim, rechecked by extracting the local PDF),
    and the safe truncation recognized in the literature requires two-level hashing or extra subkeys, none of which Poly1305 has.

### 2026-08-31

- D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) "the gain naturally disappears on small nodes" overturned by measurement: the independent variable is ε, not the node size
  - **Conclusion**: the amortization ratio is a function of ε (the fraction of internal-node bytes occupied by the buffer); the node size only sets the resolution of ε; at 16KiB, ε=0.5 amortizes over 3 entries and ε=0.95 over 57.

  - **D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes)**. Previously: "if this project lands on 16K–32K, the number of messages one flush can carry approaches 1,
    **and the gain mechanism of message buffers naturally disappears at that node size**". Now: the amortization ratio is a function of **ε (the fraction of internal-node bytes occupied by the buffer)**;
    the node size only sets the resolution of ε; at 16 KiB, ε=0.5 amortizes over 3 entries and ε=0.95 over 57.
  - **Basis**: E56 (Message Buffer Gains vs Epsilon). In the Bε arm of E7 (Offline Index Harness), buffer capacity and fanout are two unrelated constants
    (`buf_cap = 200`, `FANOUT = 32`; internal nodes hold only messages, not pivots) ⇒ the two never compete for the same node bytes,
    and that tension is the whole mechanism of Bε; its node-size sweep therefore changed node size and ε at the same time.
  - **Changed at the same time**: prerequisite 4 of D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) (node-size target line) went from open to **answered**: D8 (Core Index Structure) settled item 2
    took 16 KiB on 2026-08-30 and pinned it as a constant. New prerequisite 5 "can a message in the buffer be recomputed from units alone";
    it is now the only life-or-death prerequisite, and its authoritative record is in D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States).
  - **Another one overturned**: the crossover is not at B=F (ε=0.25). **The current direction of D8 (Core Index Structure) is itself a point on the same amortization curve**
    (write buffer of 512 entries amortized over 1024 leaves), not a "no batching" baseline ⇒ the crossover measures at **ε≈0.15**,
    and below it Bε is worse than the current direction. This was blind-derived by the forward leg of E56 (Message Buffer Gains vs Epsilon) (it gave ε=1/7≈0.143),
    and the analytic prediction the main agent wrote down before the run (crossover at ε=0.25) **was judged wrong by measurement**.
  - **Unchanged**: D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) is still pending. E56 (Message Buffer Gains vs Epsilon) only gives numbers on the gain side; cost 2 is still unquantified,
    and by the format-branch criterion of `.claude/rules/fs-design.md`, message buffers do not buy "used wrong → will not mount".
- D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) ruled: keep, ε = 0.65
  - **Conclusion**: ruled to keep, with ε=0.65; at four tree sizes the gain beats ε=0.5 at every step, and point lookups cost only about 2.4 percentage points more, but cost 2 (detectability of staleness) is still unquantified and remains the counterweight.

  - **D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes)** went from **pending** to **half-settled**. Previously: "whether to keep message buffers is unanswered".
    Now: **keep** (settled item 1), **ε = 0.65** (settled item 2, fanout 119, buffer of 665 entries).
  - **Basis**: E56 (Message Buffer Gains vs Epsilon) (N=5 seeds, range ≤3.4%). On 16 KiB nodes the gain is a strong function of ε;
    ε=0.65 at four tree sizes (1024 / 4096 / 8192 / 32768 leaves, cache share of the tree 6.4% → 0.2%) gives
    4.34× / 5.03× / 3.48× / 2.91× respectively, beating ε=0.5 at every step, and point lookups cost only about 2.4 percentage points more.
  - **The ruling was made on top of two known unresolved points, not because they went away**: cost 2 (recoverability degrading from "detectable unreachability"
    to "undetectable staleness") is still reasoning, unquantified; and the format-branch criterion of `.claude/rules/fs-design.md`
    **judges this branch a negative improvement** (it does not buy "used wrong → will not mount", and instead trades detectable unreachability for undetectable staleness);
    the same rule says explicitly "the criterion may not contain 'this is faster'" ⇒ **the gain numbers do not count as a reason to pass under that criterion**.
   ⇒ Added settled item 3 (the detection mechanism for staleness) as the counterweight to settled item 1 (open at the time, later ruled), paired with [checks-owed.md](checks-owed.md) C52 (Treating Stale as Valid).
  - **Pitfall hit**: [pitfalls.md](pitfalls.md) entry 10 (root cause "recoverability is not a design goal"). This ruling takes one step toward that root cause.
  - **Open items added at the same time**: 4 (can buffered messages be recomputed from units alone; authoritative record in D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States)),
    5 (drain contract before an index rebuild), 6 (is ε a single value or branched by layout).
  - **A piece of reasoning corrected in passing by E56 (Message Buffer Gains vs Epsilon)**: tree height is not chosen, it is a dependent variable of (leaf count, fanout);
    and **paying one more level has no decisive cost**: on 32768 leaves, ε=0.4 (no extra level) gives 1.24× and ε=0.5 (one extra level) gives 1.64×.
    The main agent had earlier recommended 0.5 because "0.5 is the largest ε that does not pay an extra level"; **that reason was judged wrong by the same batch of measurements**.
- D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes): the remaining four items ruled together, all six items settled
  - **Conclusion**: user ruling: recomputable from authoritative state, staleness detectable, draining enforced by the rebuild entry, ε a single value 0.65 with no branching; all six items of D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) are settled, and the corresponding gap in D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) is marked answered as well.

  - **Item 4 (can a message in the buffer be recomputed from units alone)** went from **open** to **settled: yes**,
    the recomputation source being "units + accounting + tombstone units" ⇒ **the buffer is still purely derived state, and D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) gains no item** (user ruling).
   **Basis**: E59 (Can Buffered Messages Recompute Solely from Units) (7 arms × 3 workload groups, byte-identical over 5 rounds, all 16 mutations caught):
    the two arms units + accounting and units + tombstone units are 0 for all four message classes; with units alone the tombstone class always collapses (resurrections = number of deletions),
    and the mapping class either cannot tell the current value (count it cannot tell = number of overwrites) or guesses wrong entry by entry when the allocator reuses low addresses.
    ⚠️ **For the narrower question "from units alone" the answer is no**: what holds is recomputation from **authoritative state**.
    ⚠️ The two premises it buys must get bodies elsewhere: "accounting can answer live-or-dead placement by placement" (D3 (Space Allocation) / D5 (Snapshot / Space Accounting Mechanism)),
   "deletion writes a tombstone unit" (D18 (Information Carried in a Block)), both user rulings.
  - **Item 3 (the detection mechanism for staleness)** went from **open** to **settled: detectable** (user ruling).
    **Basis**: the mechanism rides on the two recomputation sources of item 4: accounting answers "is this placement current",
    the tombstone unit answers "is this key dead", and no third thing is needed. The rule that detection logic may not reuse the message generation or application code is unchanged.
    ⚠️ What was ruled is "can be detected"; "proving it is detected" (inject N times, catch N times) is still owed, see C52 (Treating Stale as Valid).
  - **Item 5 (drain contract before an index rebuild)** went from **open** to **settled: draining is enforced by the rebuild entry**, not left to callers' discipline (user ruling).
    **Basis**: E56 (Message Buffer Gains vs Epsilon) measured draining as cheap (on 32768 leaves, ε=0.65: 2.62× after draining vs 2.91× without)
    ⇒ the criterion is "who enforces it", not "whether someone remembers".
  - **Item 6 (is ε a single value or branched by layout)** went from **open** to **settled: a single value 0.65, no branching** (user ruling).
    **Basis**: D14 (Dual-Track: Large/Small Files & Persistent/Transient) settled item 4 already ruled out the only candidate branching variable,
    and `.claude/rules/fs-design.md` says that when the criterion cannot be written, build only one; and ε is reversible (changing ε = rebuilding the index, no format change).
  - **The status of D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes)** went from **half-settled (four items open)** to **settled (all six items settled)**.
  - In **D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) "'loss only means slow' has one premise"**, the sentence "this item is currently unanswered" changed to answered,
    stating that "from units alone" and "from authoritative state" are two different questions with different answers.
- The two premises bought by D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) settled item 4 each return home
  - **Conclusion**: added D3 (Space Allocation) settled item 1 (allocation records determine the current version placement by placement), D18 (Information Carried in a Block) settled item 8 (tombstone units must be written), D3 (Space Allocation) settled item 2 (the tombstone cost enters the acceptance worst case); D12 (Target Media) item 4 deleted entirely.

  - **D3 (Space Allocation) adds settled item 1 (granularity of allocation records)**: **settled: placement by placement it can answer "does this placement belong to the current version"** (user ruling).
    Before: D3 (Space Allocation) had no items and said nothing about granularity; the only thing in the repo about "is this block still alive" was
    the sentence in the D18 (Information Carried in a Block) rejection list, "it is a question about a set, and a block can never answer it".
    After: the predicate has an authoritative record point, composed of two halves: the allocation records of D3 (Space Allocation) + the deadlist of D5 (Snapshot / Space Accounting Mechanism).
    **Basis**: E59 (Can Buffered Messages Recompute Solely from Units) measured that scanning units alone cannot tell apart several readable copies of the same key
    (count it cannot tell = number of overwrites), and with this predicate added the divergence of all four message classes goes to zero;
    D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) settled item 4 rests entirely on it.
  - **D18 (Information Carried in a Block) adds settled item 8 (must deletion write a tombstone unit)**: **settled: yes** (user ruling).
    Before: deletion left no trace on disk. After: write a unit whose unit type tag is "tombstone", with the same five fields of settled item 3 and no new fields.
    **Basis**: E59 (Can Buffered Messages Recompute Solely from Units) measured that when scanning units alone every deleted key resurrects (resurrections = number of deletions),

- D12 (Target Media) settled item 3 / settled item 4 each recover one real-device measurement
  - **Conclusion**: settled item 3 gains a real-device measurement: the table's byte count equals the number of devices times the entry width, and recomputation time is linear; the four comparison items of settled item 4 were each forced red on a real heterogeneous pool.

  - **Settled item 3 before**: "⚠️ **one measurement owed, E72 (Mount-Time Recalculation of Device Descriptor Table) established**: how big this table is,
    and how long per-device recomputation takes at mount; this host has no heterogeneous hardware……"
  - **Settled item 3 after**: the table's byte count is exactly `设备数 × 条目宽度` (three tiers: 2/4/8 devices); recomputation time is **linear**, with no quadratic term.
    ⚠️ The absolute millisecond values are the `sudo` overhead of the harness and may not be extrapolated; the entry width is still an assumption;
    heterogeneity covers only the one dimension `physical_block_size`.
  - **Settled item 4 before**: only one sentence of requirement: "each item must be forceable by a test into the 'mismatch' branch",
    **and none had actually been forced**.
  - **Settled item 4 after**: the four comparison items were each forced red on a **real heterogeneous pool**, **with only that one red each time**;
    the handling matches cell by cell (pbs → `refuse_rw`, capacity shrinks → `refuse`, grows → `allow_and_note`,
    identity/layout → `refuse`). **The reverse direction was also verified**: changing a quantity outside the table (readahead) still lets recomputation pass
    ⇒ the rule "what is not on the list is not compared" also has discriminative power.
  - **Basis**: E72 (Mount-Time Recalculation of Device Descriptor Table) real-device measurement, verdicts consistent over 10 rounds.
    ⚠️ **The mount path does not exist**; what was verified is whether the rule has discriminative power, not whether the implementation is right.

- D12 (Target Media) settled item 5: the first layout line is the pure-SSD branch
  - **Conclusion**: the user ruled that the first phase focuses on SSD; new settled item 5 makes the first layout line the pure-SSD branch, requiring no special interfaces such as FDP or ZNS; the conclusion of no cap in advance is unchanged.

  **User ruling: "the first phase does not care about HDD, it focuses on SSD", with the clarification "the final goal is multiple media, but the first branch is a pure-SSD branch".**

  - **Before**: D12 (Target Media) had ruled "branches open by media, no cap in advance, each layout takes one incompat bit",
    but **had never ruled which one the first version implements**: D12 (Target Media) had 4 items at the time.
  - **After**: added settled item 5: the first layout line is the **pure-SSD branch**, with the measurement basis "no FDP / ZNS / any special device interface required".
  - **Basis**: user ruling. The measurement-basis half is pinned by D26 (Background Compaction and Placement Reclamation) on the same day: it had already demoted device interfaces to
    "acceleration used when present", so requiring FDP in the first phase would contradict it.

  **This is not an overturning; it fills one cell.** Not one word of D12 (Target Media) settled item 1 (no cap in advance) changes;
  this item rules "which one the first phase builds", not "how many there are in total".

  **What it buys**: the current-phase multipliers of all 8 items in the D12 (Target Media) debt table are 1: checker, golden images, crash-point replay,
  gate wall clock are counted once in the first phase.

  **The scope narrowed in two places, and both conclusions are unchanged**: D8 (Core Index Structure) settled item 2 (16 KiB nodes) was originally supported jointly by the byte-dominated and
  seek-dominated ends; in the first phase only the byte-dominated end remains; the crossover point of D8 (Core Index Structure),
  `K/N > 顺序代价/随机代价`, takes only the SSD tier (about 10%).
  **Completely unchanged**: D13 (Verification Route) already states "rotating vs SSD lands in the device layer, not in the transaction-layer protocol"
  ⇒ the commit protocol, crash semantics and the number of structural equivalence classes (still 2) do not move at all.

  ⚠️ **A guard written into the body**: having only one layout **does not constitute** a reason to drop the incompat bit and the "device → layout" table.
  If they are dropped, when a second layout joins, an old implementation reading a new image is a **silent misread**, exactly what the basis at the start of D12 (Target Media) is meant to eliminate.

  **Chain effect**: ordinary SSDs are exactly where the original blank cell of D10 (True Answer to Random Writes / Fragmentation) sits
  ⇒ leg one of D26 (Background Compaction and Placement Reclamation) goes from "can be attached later" to the main battlefield of the first phase;
  but the "does it change the bytes of new-pool file creation" verdicts of the six open items of D26 (Background Compaction and Placement Reclamation) are unaffected, and compaction stays in the background.

- D13 (Verification Route) settled item 2 ruled: the transaction layer commits serially first
  - **Conclusion**: the user ruled serial commit first, implementing the policy of doing the slow but correct thing first; the computed crossover of single thread and fsync is about 11 thousand entries per checkpoint, and a new check that can go red watches for hitting the ceiling.

  - **Item 2** went from **open** to **settled**: **serial first** (user ruling). This implements
    `.claude/rules/fs-design.md` "先做慢而正确的那条"; it is not picking one of two paths:
    the body of D13 (Verification Route) already stated that serial is this project's mandated default.
  - **The ceiling is computed and has no safety margin**: single-thread sort-merge at 30.9–31.8M entries/s (E17 (Write Buffer Merge Limit))
    × this host's fsync at 359 µs (E44 (Host Testing and Cost of Sequence Number Bit Width)) ⇒ **crossover at about 11 thousand entries per checkpoint**;
    and the entry count at the ckpt=1000 tier in E16 (Role of Journal: WAL vs Intent Log) is of the same order of magnitude.
  - **The escape hatch exists, but it is not assumed to be enough**: E17 (Write Buffer Merge Limit) measured per-leaf partitioning parallelizable at 6.26–6.38×, to be enabled once past the crossover.
  - **Paired with a check that can go red** ⇒ added [checks-owed.md](checks-owed.md) C58 (serial commit ceiling reached with no alarm).
  - ⚠️ **No three-way argument**: this item confirms an already-written default; what truly needs a three-way round is "when to switch to parallel", and that step was not done.

- Four review items: the QEMU cell of the gate, git verification of the nine contradictions, the hollowed-out basis, and the placement of the four risks
  - **Conclusion**: review results: the root cause of the QEMU permission problem is group membership rather than ACL, now fixed; the sync direction of the nine contradictions checks out, and one ordering inversion was also caught; five bases rewritten; the four risks pinned as owed checks, no ruling changed.

  **One, gate: the QEMU cell was red all along, and the basic gate could not see it.**

  - `gate.sh` does not run the QEMU self-test by default; with `GATE_QEMU=1` **the QEMU harness goes red**.
  - The first-layer symptom was "`/dev/kvm` not readable/writable"; **the root cause was not that permission was not granted, but that it was granted the wrong way**:
    `/dev/kvm` carries `TAG+="uaccess"` (`/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/70-uaccess.rules:48`),
    and logind grants the ACL per **local seat session**, while this host uses SSH sessions ⇒ it never gets it;
    a manual `setfacl` **is cleared at the next session change**.
  - ⚠️ **The illusion it creates is the worst kind**: `--selftest` runs the VM twice, and the permission disappeared between the two runs ⇒
    the output reads "success case → 0, failure case → exit marker unreadable",
    **looking like the harness cannot tell failures apart, while actually the permission dropped**. It nearly got recorded as a harness defect.
  - **Handling**: switched to `kvm` group membership (the default udev rules already set `GROUP="kvm"`, persistent across node rebuilds).
    Under `sg kvm -c` both self-test cases judge correctly, and the full gate with `GATE_QEMU=1` has **all 33 stages green**.
  - The KVM prerequisite in [vm-harness.md](vm-harness.md) **rewritten**: it used to say "relies on ACL, works without being in the kvm group, checking the group gives the wrong conclusion";
    it now says to check the group and measure read/write, and states explicitly that `setfacl` may no longer be used to patch it.
  - **Review of D14 (Dual-Track: Large/Small Files & Persistent/Transient) settled item 1** (required by the gate stage "has an open item been settled elsewhere"):
    the conclusion is **the prerequisite is not lifted**, it stays open, and the review is written into the body. Checked by opening D15 (Format Freeze Policy) settled item 1 word for word:
    it does list the D14 (Dual-Track: Large/Small Files & Persistent/Transient) cell as "still open".

  - **The gate stage "has an open item been settled elsewhere" (`.claude/gate.d/60-stale-open-items.sh`) itself had both false reds and false greens, now fixed.**
    It fed **working-tree line numbers** straight to `git log -L`, while the line range of `-L` is interpreted against **the file in history**
    ⇒ as soon as there are uncommitted changes and a few lines have been inserted above an entry, it looks at different content in history
    (measured: line 140 in the working tree, 131 in HEAD, and 140 in HEAD is a blank line).
    **Errors in both directions have happened**: an offset that gets no timestamp ⇒ a reviewed entry reported as stale (false red);
    an offset that hits newer content ⇒ a truly stale entry let through (**the "green" earlier this round came from exactly that**).
    Two changes: ① line numbers are first mapped by content back to the HEAD version;
    ② **an uncommitted review also counts as a review**: if the entry block differs between the working tree and HEAD, it was just touched and is not stale.
    The red / green discrimination samples still judge correctly.

  - **Item 3** went from **open** to **settled**: inlining threshold **512 B** (user ruling).
  - **Basis**: round two of E68 (Selection of Inlining Threshold) (read model with cache). The pattern is "the optimal threshold = the tier where the metadata working set just fits in cache",
    and 512 B is **the fixed constant with the smallest deviation over the whole cache range**: 10% better at 16 MiB and above, 6.6% worse at the 4 MiB tier, 2.8% better at the 1 MiB tier.
  - ⚠️ **The main criterion of round one (minimum total device bytes per file) did not bracket the range**; the curve is monotonic to the endpoint:
    by bytes, inlining up to the block size always pays, because what is saved is intra-block fragmentation and what is paid is record bloat. **Recorded truthfully; the criterion was not changed.**
  - ⚠️ **The threshold is not a qualified branching variable** (measured by E8 (Different Write Paths for Large vs Small Files)) ⇒ a separate cross-threshold migration path is required,
    **split out as new settled item 5** (crash semantics of the bounded transaction inline → extent).
- D14 (Dual-Track: Large/Small Files & Persistent/Transient) settled item 3 re-judged: inlining threshold 512 B → 0 (user ruling, the criterion switched to atomicity)
  - **Conclusion**: the user re-judged the inlining threshold to 0, with small files going to separate data extents; the criterion switched from performance to atomicity, because inlining makes several files share the same atomic write unit; settled item 5 (migration semantics) therefore has no object.

  - **Before**: settled item 3 ruled "inlining threshold 512 B", based on the read model of E68 (Selection of Inlining Threshold)
    (512 B is the fixed constant with the smallest deviation over the whole cache range).
  - **After**: **threshold 0, i.e. not a single byte inlined**; small files always go to separate data extents (padded per D4 (Checksum Location) settled item 2).
  - **Basis**: **user ruling**: "small files also need atomicity; no inlining".
    **The criterion switched from performance to atomicity**: inlining crowds the data of several files into the same index node,
    so a write to one file drags the atomic units of other files on the same node, the same shape of coupling as the `pack` arm that E66 (How Small Files Land After Padding)
    knocked out, just in a different container.
    ⚠️ **Atomicity is from now on the criterion of this item itself**: any future proposal to raise the inlining threshold must first pass this gate, and performance numbers cannot answer it.
  - **Cost accepted knowingly**: a 512 B file takes 64x the space, point reads are 9.8–11.0% slower, and at cache tiers of 16 MiB and above it is 10% worse than inlining
    (E68 (Selection of Inlining Threshold)). **What it buys back**: writes 5x faster (E66 (How Small Files Land After Padding)),
    the metadata working set does not grow, and the cross-threshold migration path "inline → extent" disappears entirely.
  - **Knock-on**: settled item 5 (crash semantics of inline → extent) **has no object any more**, marked not applicable but keeping its number;
    the constraint "the threshold is not a qualified branching variable" recorded by E8 (Different Write Paths for Large vs Small Files) also no longer applies:
    with a threshold of 0 there is no threshold to cross.
  - ⚠️ **This overturns another user ruling made earlier the same day** (its original basis was the performance model of E68 (Selection of Inlining Threshold)).
    The difference between the two is not in the data but in the criterion: the earlier one asked "which threshold is fastest", this one asks "may an atomic unit be shared by several files".

  - Added D15 (Format Freeze Policy), the format freeze policy, half-settled. The basis is one round of three-way argument.
    Core mechanism: a freeze is a commit arbitrated by the gate: people decide whether to initiate it, machines decide whether it holds.
    It contains a seven-item pre-freeze list, a four-layer dependency order, a verdict table for nine kinds of post-freeze changes,
    feature bits filled out into an implementable 256-bit form (bits may not be reclaimed, because they are physical bits that really existed on disk;
    reclaiming would make that bit in an old image be misread as "new feature enabled", and the file system would really do the wrong thing),
    and two checks that can go red.

checkpoint 必须换实例代号**：当前实例没有行，谓词对它只能问「诞生代号 ≤ 挂载根 txg」，重发同一个号一发布，诞生代号等于它的孤儿全部判已发布——这是失败表能封闭的依据（D23（journal 的角色与格式） 已定项 14 的注）。**实例代号**住系统配置（E100（系统配置的三段几何） 段四那 4 字节）。可写挂载的顺序：先判这次能不能可写（可写设备数够 w 的下限 ∧ **独占打开池中过半的设备**——任意两个过半集合相交，每设备的独占打开才成为池级互斥；这条与它的代价（4 盘池只剩 2 块可写时只能只读）是 D2（RAID 条带策略） 已定项 13 定的，不是本项 ∧ 实例表可读 ∧ 实例切换的预留拿得到），再取新代号 = max(**这次挂载独占打开成功的那个集合**里各系统配置的代号（每块盘两槽里全部自证过的槽——校验和过且 fsid 与本池相同；2026-09-14 用户定案，C322（取号那一步的屏障怎么放没有条款） 三轮三方）, 根环里全部根记录的实例代号) + 1 并写进**那个集合**里的每一份系统配置、**全或无**（写系统配置与数据单元写同一个取向：一次 I/O 错要重试到 T_retry 用尽才算失败；用尽后全或无判失败时**先把已经写出的那几份回卷成旧代号**（旧代号 = 取号之前这个集合里全部自证过的槽中最大的实例代号；回卷写发生在任何单元之前），回卷不成才只读挂载——回卷期间盘上出现的「同一集合内代号不等」由 I-7.7（系统配置实例代号不低于根环） 的第 ② 句判成立（较大的号没有任何根、记录、单元带着），不另开例外，下一次挂载按 max + 1 修复；取号之后那道屏障（D23（journal 的角色与格式） 已定项 16）在任一块盘上报错同样判全或无失败，不许只重发屏障就继续；取号的写入集合与 max 的取值集合取同一个——写「全部可见」而只独占一部分时，集合外那些盘写不写得进去不由这个挂载说了算，两个挂载能互相逼成只读。**过半是准入门槛，不是写入范围**：写入集合取独占打开成功的全部设备，只写过半会把集合外的健康盘落下、它们的代号从此是旧的，与真正错过取号的盘分不开。**「可见」= 独占打开成功且系统配置读得通**；I-7.7（系统配置实例代号不低于根环） 的第 ② 句限定到同一个集合），之后才动任何单元；只读挂载不取号；从 1 起、0 无效。**前提**：同一时刻只有一个可写挂载——由过半独占打开保证；多主机共享存储上两个可写挂载会算出同一个代号、谓词分不出它们，随 D9（加密） 已定项 8 那一类宣布不防。取号那一刻两路见证不完整可见时不额外拦截，与整卷回滚同格；I-7.6（根环区域落在互不相同的盘上） 只在 devs ≥ R 时让根环成为独立见证，第一版 (R = 3, devs = 2) 不成立。错过取号的盘分两类：**打开过又掉了、且缺号期间池里确实发布过**的，回归时整盘作废、只读到重同步完成；**从未被这次挂载独占打开的**，或缺号期间池里一次发布都没有的，不作废——它没有分叉的物理可能（第八轮反推腿 3.1 / 7.2）；第一版 2 盘、掉一块只能只读挂载 ⇒ 分叉盘回归不可达；D2（RAID 条带策略） 已定项 3 / 4 允许在线加盘 ⇒ 第三块盘一加就可达，C120（分叉盘回归的判定与重同步）在允许加第三块盘之前到期，与过半规则同时。

  - **Conclusion**: filled in as object ID plus object birth generation plus the full interval, preventing an old generation's tombstone from wrongly killing a new generation's live data when the same object ID dies twice.

  - Before: the record granularity said word for word "deleting a whole object writes one interval record (object ID + full interval)".
  - Now: "object ID + object birth generation + full interval".

    and that reason holds equally for tombstone records: the same object ID dying twice (delete, recreate, delete again) cannot be told apart without the birth generation,
    and applying the old generation's tombstone would wrongly kill the new generation's live data.   - **Conclusion**: changed to eight, not in a containment relation; D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) settled item 1 rejudged as not blocking, the attribution of D13 (Verification Route) settled item 2 withdrawn, the inconsistent use of the criterion pointed out.

  **This round produces no new conclusion; it only attacks the previous round's (part seventeen) own conclusions.** Each of the three attacker legs took a group of assertions,
  and for every attack the main agent checked the facts that could discriminate before judging.

  ##### 1. Knocked out: the first version of the blocking set

  - **Before**: what must be settled before writing the first line of transaction-layer code was **exactly four**: D18 (Information Carried in a Block) settled item 3,
    D22 (Synthesizing Unit Atomicity) settled item 3, D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) settled item 1, D13 (Verification Route) settled item 2;
    **Now**: **eight**, not in a containment relation with the first version:
    D18 (Information Carried in a Block) settled item 3,
    D22 (Synthesizing Unit Atomicity) settled item 3,
    **D22 (Synthesizing Unit Atomicity) settled item 2 (root ring parameters)**,
    **D19 (Block Pointer Structure & Width Budget) settled item 3**,
    **D19 (Block Pointer Structure & Width Budget) settled item 2**,
    **D9 (Encryption) settled item 4**,
    **"how many records per transaction"** (established as D23 (Journal Role & Format) settled item 7),
    **the D5 (Snapshot / Space Accounting Mechanism) open item (counter carrier)**;
    **Basis**: the attackers gave item by item "which bytes of new-pool file creation cannot be written", and the main agent checked the original text item by item.

  - **The root cause is methodological and worth recording on its own**: **judging "not blocking" used "does it change the bytes written by new-pool file creation",
    while judging the four "blocking" ones switched to "will it go back and change a settled decision".**
    The sets measured by the two yardsticks are not in a containment relation. ⇒ **Once a criterion is written down it must be applied equally to both sides.**

  ##### 2. Two eliminated

  - **D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) settled item 1 rejudged as not blocking.**
    **Basis**: the section of D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) itself "self-containment makes half of the reverse mapping O(1)" word for word: the entire remaining duty of the reverse index is
    "answering the shared part"; and the first target has "no directories, no trees" ⇒ no shared units ⇒ entry count 0
    ⇒ the two answers are byte-identical. "If authoritative, mkfs must build a tree" is blocked by the open tree table settled by D15 (Format Freeze Policy).
  - **The attribution of D13 (Verification Route) settled item 2 withdrawn.**
    **Before**: part seventeen promoted it to a format question, saying it decides the field list of the 84-byte record header;
    **Now**: withdrawn: serial is the mandated default, and **it splits the same way under serial**;
    what really decides the record header is "how many records per transaction". It is a proxy for that gap, not the gap itself.

  ##### 3. One text conflict changed

  - **D20 (Load-Bearing Surface: Unit Atomicity & Self-Containment)**: **before** "D17 (Implementation Layering & Third-Party Pipeline) settled item 1 can be deferred until
    the first third-party pipeline appears, **or when the first line of transaction-layer code lands**"; **now** the second half deleted;
    **Basis**: what remains of D17 (Implementation Layering & Third-Party Pipeline) settled item 1 is division of labor and pricing, and division of labor only has an object when there is a second party; the first line of code produces no second party.
    Keeping it would put the item on both the "blocking" and "not blocking" sides at once.

  ##### 4. The two not knocked out, and two gaps the attackers found along the way

  - **Contradiction X (D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) cancels constraint 1 of D8 (Core Index Structure)) and contradiction Y (one transaction one record undefined) were neither knocked out**;
    the attackers tried four and three paths respectively, each failing with the reason for failure written down.
  - **Gap one**: D8 (Core Index Structure)/D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) say "rebuild the index, not rebuild the file system",
    **without connecting back the cost numbers of E29 (Blast Radius of a Single Failed Node) itself**: changing the global node size requires rebuilding the whole tree at the new size,
    on the same scale as a "bad root" (full disk scan). ⇒ What changes is the **category** (data survives), not the **cost**. Added to both bodies.
  - **Gap two**: E28 (Can Plaintext Mapping Rebuild Solely from Self-Describing Units) tested **the plaintext mapping layer**,
    while D8 (Core Index Structure)/D11 (Message Buffers in Index Nodes) applied it to rebuilding **the index tree**;
    **the bridge was never argued**. The argument has been added in D8 (Core Index Structure) (both read the same unit self-description),
    marking that **that step is reasoning, not measurement**.

    It also states that 32 bits is exactly the width of a full CRC32C, and **the implementation may not go via "a wider CRC truncated to 32 bits"**:
    E40 (Ciphertext Checksum Bit Width) measured that truncation degrades single-bit flips from always detected to probabilistically detected.

- D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) settled item 5 settled: allocation records are derived state, C73 (Allocation record state classification unsettled) closed, at the cost of the level-2 promotion of D18 (Information Carried in a Block) losing its witness
  - **Conclusion**: D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) adds settled item 5: allocation records are derived state, and authoritative state remains the three things units, accounting and roots; as a knock-on, one promotion mechanism loses its witness.

  **Before**: settled item 1 of D3 (Space Allocation) said verbatim that allocation records are the "authoritative record point" of the predicate
  "does a given placement belong to the current version at this moment", while settled item 3 of D3 (Space Allocation) settled that they live in a btree with its own keyspace, and per D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States)
  trees are derived state. One place said authoritative, the other's classification said derived; the two claims coexisted with nobody closing them, registered in C73 (Allocation record state classification unsettled).

  **After**: D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) adds settled item 5: **allocation records are derived state**, and authoritative state remains
  the three things "units + accounting + roots", with no item added. The two sentences do not contradict, because they answer two questions: "whom to ask at runtime"
  is the runtime basis (no live scanning; there must be an answer at the moment of asking), while "can it come back if lost" is the recovery basis (state class).
  The rebuild source is the same set E59 (Can Buffered Messages Recompute Solely from Units) measured (units + accounting ⇒ all four kinds of divergence go to zero).
  The related notes in settled item 1 of D3 (Space Allocation) and settled item 3 of D18 (Information Carried in a Block) rewritten accordingly, and C73 (Allocation record state classification unsettled) marked paid off.

  **Four consequences recorded as they are**: ① its format may change freely and does not take part in the layer-2 freeze of D15 (Format Freeze Policy);
  ② but it must satisfy the D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) supplement "corruption of derived state must be detectable",
  and allocation records do not yet have a detection mechanism; ③ **the level-2 promotion of `map_provenance` in settled item 3 of D18 (Information Carried in a Block)
  loses its witness**: C73 (Allocation record state classification unsettled) verbatim "something in derived state must itself be rebuilt and cannot serve as a witness",
  so level 2 must find another double witness living in authoritative state or that cell reopens; levels 1 and 0 are unaffected;
  ④ chains to settled item 5 of D26 (Background Compaction and Placement Reclamation): relocation forwarding information is a historical event and cannot be scan-rebuilt
  ⇒ **forwarding cannot live only in allocation records**: either make it units entering authoritative state (the same device as the tombstones of settled item 10 of D18 (Information Carried in a Block)),
  or go back to one of the two old routes, "change K snapshot trees" or "pin the old placement".

  **Basis**: user settlement ("分配记录 是派生态"). The mechanism basis is D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States)'s
  own three settled boundaries: authoritative state is verbatim "units + accounting + roots", allocation records are not among them, and their whole tree can be rebuilt from these three.

### 2026-08-31

- "Losing it only makes it slower" of D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States) gains its precondition: corruption must be detectable
  - **Conclusion**: precondition added: these two sentences hold only when corruption can be noticed by the system; if a format choice degrades corruption from detectable unreachability to undetectable staleness, the two sentences no longer apply.

  - **D21 (Boundary Between Authoritative and Derived States)**. Before: the classification table said "derived state (indexes): losing it only makes it slower. Does not take part in format freeze",
    and the body said "the format of derived state may change freely, because it can all be rebuilt from units", **both sentences unconditional**.

    neighbouring slots within the same chunk 10/10 intact, two cross-region regions 10/10 intact. ⇒ **exposure surface ≠ loss surface; 16 is an upper bound.**

    Basis: E42 (Number of Records per Transaction) measured that both routes satisfy I-4.3 (Atomic Commit) (one record per transaction: 0/201 illegal;
    multiple records without boundary fields: **1400/1601 = 87.4%** illegal; with boundary fields back to 0/1601),
    **the experiment cannot tell right from wrong**, and the user settled on the more general one: "one record per transaction" turns
    "every operation must be splittable into transactions that each fit in one record" into a hard constraint nobody guarantees today, and also
    pushes the ring larger via I-8.1 (Ring Geometry Sufficiently Large).
    ⚠️ **The direction of convergence of two wordings is settled accordingly**: the "worst journal **occupancy**" of I-8.1 (Ring Geometry Sufficiently Large) is right;
    deadlock 3 of D23 (Journal Role & Format), "split into several individually legal transactions", **is no longer read as "one record per transaction"**.
    **Three obligations** (user settlement: the algorithm must be strengthened): ① add a transaction number and commit marker to the 84-byte header;
    ② after "contiguous + checksum + reverse chain", the recovery algorithm **adds one more step discarding the uncommitted tail**:
    **the reverse chain cannot do it**, since the discarded tail is contiguous on the chain; ③ the criterion must be written as an invariant, landing in C37 (transaction to record mapping undefined).
    ⚠️ **Discarding the tail is the normal case, not a corner** (87.4%), and must be covered by crash-point replay just like the main path.

  - **D23 (Journal Role & Format) settled item 8: "add it or not" settled: add a reverse chain. Width still unsettled, candidate 32 bits.**
    Basis: E39 (Does Reverse Chain Block Remnant Records) measured: in the 16 cells with the chain on, residues are all 0 with no false kills;
    2 million independent trials per width class, **the measurements hug 2⁻ⁿ class by class**:
    8 bits 3961 ppm (+1 byte), 16 bits 16 ppm (+2 bytes), 32 bits 0 (+4 bytes, header grows 4.76%).
    ⚠️ Transaction number / commit marker / reverse chain are **three different fields** and may not be priced together.

### 2026-08-28

- Added D22 (Synthesizing Unit Atomicity): the dividing line is that a unit counts as published only when, after landing on disk, there is a parent pointer carrying its checksum.
  - **Conclusion**: added D22 (Synthesizing Unit Atomicity): the dividing line is that a unit counts as published only when, after landing on disk, there is a parent pointer carrying its checksum.
  - **Conclusion**: both overturned: the circular argument does not hold; D16 (Publish Semantics) has settled the journal as a hard requirement that cannot be bypassed; six unsettled items added.

  - Added D22 (Synthesizing Unit Atomicity), how unit atomicity is synthesised (three-way argument + main agent ruling). Dividing line settled:
    whether, after a unit lands on disk, there is a parent pointer carrying its checksum before it counts as published.
  - **Overturned one sentence written this round**: it once judged "choosing COW-allocated journal segments bypasses tear detection";
    the basis for overturning it is a circular argument: COWing a record needs a pointer to it, the pointer needs committing,
    and committing is exactly the job of the journal; moreover a non-ring journal does one root write per record,
    while the whole benefit of the journal is amortising root writes. **A journal covered by COW buys nothing.**
  - **Overturned one row of the forward leg**: it judged the journal covered by COW, on the grounds that this project has no second transaction mechanism.
    The rule was cited right but the fact was wrong: D16 (Publish Semantics) has settled that we have a journal, and it is a hard requirement that "no operation may bypass it".
  - **Overturned a reading of a wording in D12 (Target Media)**: the kind that "can overwrite the root pointer in place" actually cannot overwrite the only copy either,
    and can only rotate within a fixed slot group + carry a number. Both kinds of layout need the same root mechanism,
    which narrows the D16 (Publish Semantics) gap "the redundancy form of the root itself".
  - Six unsettled items added, all surfaced in this round and absent from the kb before: whether the journal is a ring,
    root ring parameters and the failure domain independence assumption, whether accounting is COW, whether "blocks released within this transaction must not be reused" exists,
    the measurement basis of D2 (RAID Stripe Policy) must expand to "does not induce device RMW", and the zoned write pointer is a witness not governed by our checksums.

### 2026-08-28

- The way out of deadlock 2 of D23 (Journal Role & Format) corrected: the reserve pool changed to a computable admission rule.

  - **The way out of deadlock 2 of D23 (Journal Role & Format) corrected**: it said "there must be a reserve pool" (citing btrfs's global_block_rsv),
    while E19 (Spurious ENOSPC Under Defer Window) measured that a reserve pool cannot save it: reserving 0→16384 blocks, the checkpoint stall count did not budge (199→200),
    and spurious ENOSPC instead rose from 3150 to 7246. The mechanism is that the stall comes from the amount held by defer/K itself exceeding the remaining space,
    while global_block_rsv guards against normal allocation eating up the space.
    Changed to **a computable admission rule**: remaining space > churn × (delay+1) + checkpoint overhead,
    and E19 (Spurious ENOSPC Under Defer Window) across 6 fill rates × 6 delays, 36 cells in all, matched prediction and measurement cell by cell.

    "replacing cycle with txg" moves only axis ① (sequence identity), while axis ② (stamping every 512 bytes) is an independent choice,
    which buys deterministic tear detection vs a 2⁻ⁿ probability; the right reason for not doing it is "2⁻³² is small enough".
    ② "the journal cannot be covered by COW" holds only for a fixed-length ring: ZFS's ZIL is chained,
    with each block's trailer carrying a blkptr to the next block, the cycle broken by "the pointer living in the previous record".

    with AES-NI, 16 cores give about 62 GB/s, above any single device ⇒ the GPU is most likely useless for the scrub cell;
    **without AES-NI, 16 cores give about 4.3 GB/s, and that class is the only entry for the GPU supported by data**.
- The multi-core class of E6 (Encryption Algorithm Selection) run in addition, and the conclusion of D24 (Offloading Heavy Background Work to GPU) flipped by measurement
  - **Conclusion**: the multi-core measurement of E6 (Encryption Algorithm Selection) saturates AES-256-GCM at 17.4 GB/s with 8 threads, below both GPU floors, so the judgment changed to GPU wins.

  - **D24 (Offloading Heavy Background Work to GPU) "with AES-NI ⇒ GPU offload is a negative gain": once a verdict, now the direction is reversed.**
    **Used to be**: the CPU side plugged in "single core 3888.51 MiB/s × 16 cores ≈ 65 GB/s" ⇒ above the GPU's 56.7, the GPU loses;
    **Now**: the multi-core class of E6 (Encryption Algorithm Selection) measured **AES-256-GCM saturating at 17.4 GB/s with 8 threads** (16.3/16.5 at 16/32 threads),
    below both GPU floors (round trip 28.5, one way 50.3) ⇒ **the GPU wins**;
    **Basis**: `scripts/experiment-apparatus/e6_multicore.rs`, both positive controls pass
    (single core reproduces E6 (Encryption Algorithm Selection) within 11.0%, the compute-bound arm 15.31×).
    ⚠️ **This may not be flipped into "the GPU always wins"**: the 50.3 GB/s of E21 (Net Benefit of GPU Offloading) used a bandwidth-bound operator as the kernel,
    while a real AES-GCM kernel is heavier; a verdict still needs `nvcc`.
  - **"Whether the bottleneck is the CPU is equivalent to whether there are hardware instructions" falls at the same time.**
    **Basis**: encryption with AES-NI still saturates at 17.4 GB/s, and the bottleneck remains on the CPU side.

The gain measure of point 7 extended to all background tasks, stating that the purpose of the GPU is to take less host CPU time, and being faster with large data volumes is only a by-product. The scope states that points 5 and 6 govern only GC, and the three candidates of D24 (Offloading Heavy Background Work to GPU) join the same set of switches when reopened, to be settled when the criterion is reopened. The scope at the opening of D24 (Offloading Heavy Background Work to GPU) changed by one sentence accordingly.
  - **Basis**: user settlement. The trigger was that milestone 7 added GPU packing relocation (`.claude/kb/milestone/07-seventh-txn.md` "三　GPU 打包搬迁"), and the main agent asked whether parameters are shared or one set each, and by which criterion it is judged worth it.
